In this article AMZN MSFT GOOGL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A sign on the Microsoft campus in Redmond, Washington, US, Oct. 26, 2026. David Ryder | Reuters Microsoft suffered a widespread outage on Thursday that impacted thousands of users across regions, according to outage-tracking website Downdetector.com . The outage began shortly before 1 p.m. and affected services Microsoft 365 services, Outlook. Amazon Web Services and Google users also reported outages on the site. "We are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with Microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with Exchange Online," a Microsoft spokesperson wrote in a statement to CNBC. "We appreciate our customers' patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible." Microsoft initially wrote in a post to its Microsoft 365 Status account on X that the connectivity problems may stem from some infrastructure "elevated load across multiple regions." The company later determined that the elevated load was caused by a "number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure." "We've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being impacted while we work to return the affected servers to service," Microsoft wrote . Executives will announce a new relationship with Microsoft , one of the world's top cloud providers, on a conference call with analysts, Feldman said. The call starts at 5 p.m. ET. Cerebras has also landed deals with other major cloud providers Amazon and Oracle . Cerebras is evaluating its financing options to meet the ramping demand, Feldman said in the interview. The computer networking company is trying to become a bigger player in AI after missing out on the early years of the boom. The stock is up 35% this year, trouncing the Nasdaq, which is up about 9%. In this article CSCO Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins appears at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, on Jan. 21, 2026. Krisztian Bocsi | Bloomberg | Getty Images Cisco shares rose in extended trading on Thursday after the maker of networking gear reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter results. Here's how the company did compared to LSEG consensus estimates: EPS: $1.40 adjusted vs. $1.33 expected Revenue: $18.5 billion vs. $18.1 billion expected. Revenue increased 24% from $14.88 billion a year earlier, Cisco said in a statement. Net income rose to $4.6 billion, or $1.14 per share, from $2.9 billion, or 72 center per share, a year ago. Cisco is trying to gain a foothold in the artificial intelligence buildout after missing out on the early years of the generative AI boom. The company's stock price is up about 35% this year as of Thursday's close, trouncing the Nasdaq, which has gained 9% over that stretch. Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9 billion this fiscal year, more than double the figure in fiscal 2026. "Organizations are turning to Cisco for our trusted, market-defining technology and our expertise to help them scale, secure and optimize their environments for the agentic AI era," CEO Chuck Robbins said in the statement . For the fiscal second quarter, Cisco said it expects revenue of between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, topping the average analyst estimate of $17.88 billion, according to LSEG. The company is projecting adjusted earnings per share of $1.34 to $1.36, beating the $1.23 average estimate.
